specification.scope: Original WBXBAR public bus boundary, revision 2e8d3bc2d26ddc33d1881022a2a2b9d3f0c16b9b. Two masters, two slaves. No internal state or submodule observation.

authority.representation: Maintainer paraphrase checked against PDF pages 31–38; not a new protocol specification.

requirements.summary: Reset takes effect on rising clock edges. Hold reset for at least one complete cycle. Master CYC and STB are inactive during reset; other master payload values are unspecified.
CYC qualifies bus activity and spans a transfer cycle. Without CYC, slave request signals are inactive. System reset remains effective.

Pipelined acceptance requires CYC and STB high and STALL low. WE distinguishes writes from reads. New requests need not wait for earlier acknowledgments. ACK can occur while STB is low. Successful transactions retire with acknowledgments; read data is meaningful with ACK.
ERR reports failure; the base protocol leaves the master reaction unspecified. ACK, ERR and RTY cannot coincide. Payload belongs to a strobed request. This interface has no RTY signal.

188: - [WBXBAR](rtl/wbxbar.v) is a fully function N master to M slave Wishbone
189:   [crossbar](https://zipcpu.com/blog/2019/07/17/crossbar.html).  Unlike my
190:   Unlike my [earlier WB interconnects](https://zipcpu.com/blog/2017/06/22/simple-wb-interconnect.html), this one guarantees that the
191:   ACK responses won't get crossed, and that misbehaving slave accesses will
192:   be timed out.  The core also has options for checking for starvation
193:   (where a master's request is not granted in a particular period of time),
194:   double-buffering all outputs (i.e. with [skid
195:   buffers](https://zipcpu.com/blog/2019/05/22/skidbuffer.html), and forcing idle
196:   channel values to zero in order to reduce power.

7: // Purpose:	A Configurable wishbone cross-bar interconnect, conforming
8: //		to the WB-B4 pipeline specification, as described on the
9: //	ZipCPU blog.
10: //
11: // Performance:
12: //	Throughput: One transaction per clock
13: //	Latency: One clock to get access to an unused channel, another to
14: //	place the results on the slave bus, and another to return, or a minimum
15: //	of three clocks.
16: //
17: // Usage: To use, you'll need to set NM and NS to the number of masters
18: //	(input ports) and the number of slaves respectively.  You'll then
19: //	want to set the addresses for the slaves in the SLAVE_ADDR array,
20: //	together with the SLAVE_MASK array indicating which SLAVE_ADDRs
21: //	are valid.  Address and data widths should be adjusted at the same
22: //	time.
23: //
24: //	Voila, you are now set up!
25: //
26: //	Now let's fine tune this:
27: //
28: //	LGMAXBURST can be set to control the maximum number of outstanding
29: //	transactions.  An LGMAXBURST of 6 will allow 63 outstanding
30: //	transactions.
31: //
32: //	OPT_TIMEOUT, if set to a non-zero value, is a number of clock periods
33: //	to wait for a slave to respond.  Should the timeout expire and the
34: //	slave not respond, a bus error will be returned and the slave will
35: //	be issued a bus abort signal (CYC will be dropped).
36: //
37: //	OPT_STARVATION_TIMEOUT, if set, applies the OPT_TIMEOUT counter to
38: //	how long a particular master waits for arbitration.  If the master is
39: //	"starved", a bus error will be returned.

authority.representation: Prose-only intent paraphrase; no implementation examples, expressions or internal signal names included. Older design article is supplementary, not exact-cycle authority.

requirements.location: What is a Crossbar?; Returning data, paragraphs on nonexistent addresses and abort
requirements.summary: A crossbar connects masters to slaves without mixing their responses. A request outside every configured address range should return an error. A master may end its cycle to abort outstanding work; completed data must not later be attributed to a new transaction. The article motivates aborting a cycle after an error. Exact buffering, arbitration and timeout edge counts require explicit documentation rather than assumptions.

interface.packing: Port 0 occupies the least-significant slice. Each address is an 8-bit bus address, each data value 32 bits, each select 4 bits. No implicit byte-address shifting.
interface.address_configuration: Slave0: (addr & 0xf0)==0x00; slave1: (addr & 0xf0)==0x10. Other addresses match neither slave. This is public parameter decoding, not stimulus guidance.
interface.directions: i_m* are external master inputs; o_m* are DUT responses. o_s* are DUT requests to external slaves; i_s* are external slave responses. i_clk is the common clock.
interface.rows: [{cycle:int, pre:{all listed inputs and outputs}, post:{all listed outputs}}]; integers of declared width. None may represent undefined inactive payload, never a valid active control/data value.
interface.sampling: Inputs change while clock low. Pre sampled at +4ns, rising edge at +5ns, post at +9ns, falling edge at +10ns. One row is one physical cycle. Initial trace has two reset cycles followed by quiescence. No extra hidden clock edges.
interface.boundary: Checker consumes actual public-pin observations, not model offers or driver queue ledgers. Drivers may queue offers and hold pins through acceptance. Do not trust driver internal accounting as functional truth.
interface.environment_contract: External masters obey pipelined acceptance, holding pending request payload through backpressure except explicit cycle abort/reset. External slaves respond in acceptance order, may wait, and do not generate unsolicited responses. Slave work is canceled on cycle withdrawal/reset. Record violations separately from DUT faults. Exact future JSON offer fields are irrelevant to the pin-based checker.

requested_obligations: mapped request routing and payload/byte-mask preservation
response order, destination and read-data preservation across concurrent masters
no invented/duplicated successful transaction, reset and abort epoch separation
unmapped/slave-error response and subsequent restart; timeout scope explicitly justified
specification.isolation: No executable DUT RTL, prior checker, calibrated traces, source targets, coverage results, semantic equivalences or model outcomes.

Wishbone B4


Chapter 3. WISHBONE Classic Bus Cycles
WISHBONE Classic bus cycles are described in terms of their general operation, reset
operation, handshaking protocol and the data organization during transfers. Additional
requirements for bus cycles (especially those relating to the common clock) can be found in
the timing specifications in Chapter 5.
3.1     General Operation
MASTER and SLAVE interfaces are interconnected with a set of signals that permit them
to exchange data. For descriptive purposes these signals are cumulatively known as a bus,
and are contained within a functional module called the INTERCON. Address, data and
other information is impressed upon this bus in the form of bus cycles.

3.1.1     Reset Operation
All hardware interfaces are initialized to a pre-defined state. This is accomplished with the
reset signal [RST_O] that can be asserted at any time. It is also used for test simulation
purposes by initializing all self-starting state machines and counters which may be used in
the design. The reset signal [RST_O] is driven by the SYSCON module. It is connected to
the [RST_I] signal on all MASTER and SLAVE interfaces. Illustration 3-1: Reset cycle
shows the reset cycle.


                                                              NOTE(2)
                                  CLK_I           0                1    NOTE(1)    2                3




                 MASTER SIGNALS
                                  RST_I
                                                                                                  NOTE(3)
                                  STB_O


                                  CYC_O

                                          NOTES:
                                          (1) Reset cycles can be extended for any length of time.
                                          (2) Self-starting state machines & counters reset themselves at
                                              the rising [CLK_I] edge following the assertion of [RST_I].
                                              On MASTERs,[STB_O] and [CYC_O] are negated at the same time.
                                          (3) On MASTERs, [STB_O] and [CYC_O] may be asserted at the
                                              rising [CLK_I] edge following the negation of [RST_I].

                                              Illustration 3-1: Reset cycle

   RULE 3.00
All WISHBONE interfaces MUST initialize themselves at the rising [CLK_I] edge following
the assertion of [RST_I]. They MUST stay in the initialized state until the rising [CLK_I]
edge that follows the negation of [RST_I].

   RULE 3.05
[RST_I] MUST be asserted for at least one complete clock cycle on all WISHBONE
interfaces.

   PERMISSION 3.00
[RST_I] MAY be asserted for more than one clock cycle, and MAY be asserted indefinitely.


     Back to TOC                                Copyright © 2010 OpenCores                                   Page 31 / 128

Wishbone B4


   RULE 3.10
All WISHBONE interfaces MUST be capable of reacting to [RST_I] at any time.

   RULE 3.15
All self-starting state machines and counters in WISHBONE interfaces MUST initialize
themselves at the rising [CLK_I] edge following the assertion of [RST_I]. They MUST stay
in the initialized state until the rising [CLK_I] edge that follows the negation of [RST_I].

   OBSERVATION 3.00
In general, self-starting state machines do not need to be initialized. However, this may
cause problems because some simulators may not be sophisticated enough to find an initial
starting point for the state machine. Furthermore, self-starting state machines can go
through an indeterminate number of initialization cycles before finding their starting state,
thereby making it difficult to predict their behavior at start-up time. The initialization rule
prevents both problems by forcing all state machines to a pre-defined state in response to
the assertion of [RST_I].

   RULE 3.20
The following MASTER signals MUST be negated at the rising [CLK_I] edge following the
assertion of [RST_I], and MUST stay in the negated state until the rising [CLK_I] edge
that follows the negation of [RST_I]: [STB_O], [CYC_O]. The state of all other MASTER
signals are undefined in response to a reset cycle.

   OBSERVATION 3.05
On MASTER interfaces [STB_O] and [CYC_O] may be asserted beginning at the rising
[CLK_I] edge following the negation of [RST_I].


   OBSERVATION 3.10
SLAVE interfaces automatically negate [ACK_O], [ERR_O] and [RTY_O] when their
[STB_I] is negated in standard mode.
In pipelined mode the assertion of [ACK_O], [ERR_O] and [RTY_O] is done
independently of [STB_I].

   RECOMENDATION 3.00
Design SYSCON modules so that they assert [RST_O] during a power-up condition.
[RST_O] should remain asserted until all voltage levels and clock frequencies in the system
are stabilized. When negating [RST_O], do so in a synchronous manner that conforms to
this specification.

   OBSERVATION 3.15
If a gated clock generator is used, and if the clock is stopped, then the WISHBONE
interface is not capable of responding to its [RST_I] signal.

   SUGGESTION 3.00
Some circuits require an asynchronous reset capability. If an IP core or other SoC
component requires an asynchronous reset, then define it as a non-WISHBONE signal.
This prevents confusion with the WISHBONE reset [RST_I] signal that uses a purely
synchronous protocol, and needs to be applied to the WISHBONE interface only.


     Back to TOC               Copyright © 2010 OpenCores                Page 32 / 128

Wishbone B4


   OBSERVATION 3.20
All WISHBONE interfaces respond to the reset signal. However, the IP Core connected to
a WISHBONE interface does not necessarily need to respond to the reset signal.

3.1.2     Transfer Cycle initiation
MASTER interfaces initiate a transfer cycle by asserting [CYC_O]. When [CYC_O] is
negated, all other MASTER signals are invalid.
SLAVE interfaces respond to other SLAVE signals only when [CYC_I] is asserted.
SYSCON signals and responses to SYSCON signals are not affected.

   RULE 3.25
MASTER interfaces MUST assert [CYC_O] for the duration of SINGLE READ / WRITE,
BLOCK and RMW cycles. [CYC_O] MUST be asserted no later than the rising [CLK_I]
edge that qualifies the assertion of [STB_O]. [CYC_O] MUST be negated no earlier than
the rising [CLK_I] edge that qualifies the negation of [STB_O].

   PERMISSION 3.05
MASTER interfaces MAY assert [CYC_O] indefinitely.

   RECOMMENDATION 3.05
Arbitration logic often uses [CYC_I] to select between MASTER interfaces. Keeping
[CYC_O] asserted may lead to arbitration problems. It is therefore recommended that
[CYC_O] is not indefinitely asserted.

   RULE 3.30
SLAVE interfaces MAY NOT respond to any SLAVE signals when [CYC_I] is negated.
However, SLAVE interfaces MUST always respond to SYSCON signals.

3.1.3     Handshaking Protocol
All bus cycles use a handshaking protocol between the MASTER and SLAVE interfaces.
There exists two different traffic modes, standard and pipelined.

3.1.3.1   Standard wishbone protocol

As shown in Figure 3-2, the MASTER asserts [STB_O] when it is ready to transfer data.
[STB_O] remains asserted until the SLAVE asserts one of the cycle terminating signals
[ACK_I], [ERR_I] or [RTY_I]. At every rising edge of [CLK_I] the terminating signal is
sampled. If it is asserted, then [STB_O] is negated. This gives both MASTER and SLAVE
interfaces the possibility to control the rate at which data is transferred.




        Illustration 3-2: Standard bus handshaking protocol, asynchronous slave.



     Back to TOC              Copyright © 2010 OpenCores            Page 33 / 128

Wishbone B4




      Illustration 3-3: Standard wishbone handshaking protocol, synchronous slave.



   PERMISSION 3.10
If in standard mode the SLAVE guarantees it can keep pace with all MASTER interfaces
and if the [ERR_I] and [RTY_I] signals are not used, then the SLAVE’s [ACK_O] signal
MAY be tied to the logical AND of the SLAVE’s [STB_I] and [CYC_I] inputs. The interface
will function normally under these circumstances.

   OBSERVATION 3.25
In standard mode SLAVE interfaces assert a cycle termination signal in response to
[STB_I]. However, [STB_I] is only valid when [CYC_I] is valid.

   RULE 3.35
In standard mode the cycle termination signals [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] must be
generated in response to the logical AND of [CYC_I] and [STB_I].

   PERMISSION 3.15
Other signals, besides [CYC_I] and [STB_I], MAY be included in the generation of the
cycle termination signals.

   OBSERVATION 3.30
Internal SLAVE signals also determine what cycle termination signal is asserted and when
it is asserted.
Most of the examples in this specification describe the use of [ACK_I] to terminate a local
bus cycle. However, the SLAVE can optionally terminate the cycle with an error [ERR_O],
or request that the cycle be retried [RTY_O].
All MASTER interfaces include the [ACK_I] terminator signal. Asserting this signal during
a bus cycle causes it to terminate normally.
Asserting the [ERR_I] signal during a bus cycle will terminate the cycle. It also serves to
notify the MASTER that an error occurred during the cycle. This signal is generally used if
an error was detected by SLAVE logic circuitry. For example, if the SLAVE is a parity-
protected memory, then the [ERR_I] signal can be asserted if a parity fault is detected.
This specification does not dictate what the MASTER will do in response to [ERR_I].
Asserting the optional [RTY_I] signal during a bus cycle will terminate the cycle. It also
serves to notify the MASTER that the current cycle should be aborted, and retried at a later
time. This signal is generally used for shared memory and bus bridges. In these cases
SLAVE circuitry asserts [RTY_I] if the local resource is busy. This specification does not
dictate when or how the MASTER will respond to [RTY_I].

   RULE 3.40
As a minimum, the MASTER interface MUST include the following signals: [ACK_I],


     Back to TOC               Copyright © 2010 OpenCores              Page 34 / 128

Wishbone B4


[CLK_I], [CYC_O], [RST_I], and [STB_O]. As a minimum, the SLAVE interface MUST
include the following signals: [ACK_O], [CLK_I], [CYC_I], [STB_I], and [RST_I]. All
other signals are optional.

   PERMISSION 3.20
MASTER and SLAVE interfaces MAY be designed to support the [ERR_I] and [ERR_O]
signals. In these cases, the SLAVE asserts [ERR_O] to indicate that an error has occurred
during the bus cycle. This specification does not dictate what the MASTER does in
response to [ERR_I].

   PERMISSION 3.25
MASTER and SLAVE interfaces MAY be designed to support the [RTY_I] and [RTY_O]
signals. In these cases, the SLAVE asserts [RTY_O] to indicate that the interface is busy,
and that the bus cycle should be retried at a later time. This specification does not dictate
what the MASTER will do in response to [RTY_I].

   RULE 3.45
If a SLAVE supports the [ERR_O] or [RTY_O] signals, then the SLAVE MUST NOT assert
more than one of the following signals at any time: [ACK_O], [ERR_O] or [RTY_O].

   OBSERVATION 3.35
If the SLAVE supports the [ERR_O] or [RTY_O] signals, but the MASTER does not
support these signals, deadlock may occur.

   RECOMMENDATION 3.10
Design INTERCON modules to prevent deadlock conditions. One solution to this problem
is to include a watchdog timer function that monitors the MASTER’s [STB_O] signal, and
asserts [ERR_I] or [RTY_I] if the cycle exceeds some pre-defined time limit. INTERCON
modules can also be designed to disconnect interfaces from the WISHBONE bus if they
constantly generate bus errors and/or watchdog time-outs.

   RECOMMENDATION 3.15
Design WISHBONE MASTER interfaces so that there are no intermediate logic gates
between a registered flip-flop and the signal outputs on [STB_O] and [CYC_O]. Delay
timing for [STB_O] and [CYC_O] are very often the most critical paths in the system. This
prevents sloppy design practices from slowing down the interconnect because of added
delays on these two signals.

   RULE 3.50
SLAVE interfaces MUST be designed so that the [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] signals
are asserted and negated in response to the assertion and negation of [STB_I].

   PERMISSION 3.30
The assertion of [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] MAY be asynchronous to the [CLK_I]
signal (i.e. there is a combinatorial logic path between [STB_I] and [ACK_O]).

   OBSERVATION 3.40
The asynchronous assertion of [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] assures that the
interface can accomplish one data transfer per clock cycle. Furthermore, it simplifies the
design of arbiters in multi-MASTER applications.

     Back to TOC               Copyright © 2010 OpenCores                Page 35 / 128

Wishbone B4


   OBSERVATION 3.45
The asynchronous assertion of [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] could proof impossible
to implement. For example slave wait states are easiest implemented using a registered
[ACK_O] signal.

   OBSERVATION 3.50
In large high speed designs the asynchronous assertion of [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and
[RTY_O] could lead to unacceptable delay times, caused by the loopback delay from the
MASTER to the SLAVE and back to the MASTER. Using registered [ACK_O], [ERR_O],
and [RTY_O] signals significantly reduces this loopback delay, at the cost of one additional
wait state per transfer. See WISHBONE Registered Feedback Bus Cycles for methods of
eliminating the wait state.

   PERMISSION 3.35
Under certain circumstances SLAVE interfaces MAY be designed to hold [ACK_O] in the
asserted state. This situation occurs on point-to-point interfaces where there is a single
SLAVE on the interface, and that SLAVE always operates without wait states.

   RULE 3.55
MASTER interfaces MUST be designed to operate normally when the SLAVE interface
holds [ACK_I] in the asserted state.

3.1.3.2     Pipelined wishbone protocol

In pipelined mode the handshake protocol is somewhat different.
   ●    The master doesn't wait for [ACK_I] before outputting next address/data word on
        the bus
   ●    we have a [STALL_I] input in the master, indicating that the slave pipeline can
        accept another request at the moment. For a bus arbiter a multiplexer should be
        used to select the targeted slave [STALL_O] signal and feed that to the master. This
        path should be non registered.
   ●    master outputs the requests as long as [STALL_I] is low. When [STALL_I] is
        asserted, it waits. Also, the pipeline in the interconnect doesn't push any requests
        when [STALL_I] is asserted.
   ●    cycle consisting of N transactions is terminated with a sequence of N [ACK_I].
        Subsequent [ACK_I] indicate the finished transactions. Master terminates the bus
        cycle (by deasserting [CYC_O]) after receiving the last [ACK_I] pulse.
   ●    read data is valid when [ACK_I] is high.




       Back to TOC              Copyright © 2010 OpenCores               Page 36 / 128

Wishbone B4




                       Illustration 3-4: Pipelined mode, single access



   RULE 3.57
In pipelined mode a read transaction is started when the following signals are asserted
       [CYC_I], [STB_I]
and the following negated
       [STALL_I], [WE_I].

   RULE 3.58
In pipelined mode a write transaction is started when the following signals are asserted
       [CYC_I], [STB_I], [WE_I]
and the following negated
       [STALL_I].

   RULE 3.59
In pipelined mode the MASTER must accept [ACK_I] signals at any time after a
transaction is initiated.

3.1.4     Use of [STB_O]

   RULE 3.60
MASTER interfaces MUST qualify the following signals with [STB_O]: [ADR_O],
[DAT_O()], [SEL_O()], [WE_O], and [TAGN_O].

   PERMISSION 3.40
If a MASTER doesn’t generate wait states, then [STB_O] and [CYC_O] MAY be assigned
the same signal.

   OBSERVATION 3.55
[CYC_O] needs to be asserted during the entire transfer cycle. A MASTER that doesn’t
generate wait states doesn’t negate [STB_O] during a transfer cycle, i.e. it is asserted the
entire transfer cycle. Therefore it is allowed to use the same signal for [CYC_O] and
[STB_O]. Both signals must be present on the interface though.




     Back to TOC               Copyright © 2010 OpenCores                Page 37 / 128

wishbone_primary_text.note: Full relevant pages; distinguish standard and pipelined rules. Figures extracted as text may lose alignment; no exact latency inferred from figure text.

supplementary_abort_prose.locations: discussion of bus abort; Returning data
supplementary_abort_prose.authority_level: Older explanatory article, not a version-specific cancellation timing contract
supplementary_abort_prose.paraphrase: The author describes dropping CYC after an error to abort outstanding work; pending transactions have uncertain status. Slave-side cycle withdrawal follows upstream abort. No further response should be attributed to the aborted master cycle. The prose does not specify which buffered requests survive partial propagation or a fixed bound on observing residual forwarding. Code examples are excluded from this specification-only packet.

clause_matrix.observables: pre.i_reset; post.o_scyc and post.o_sstb at the reset edge; i_mcyc and i_mstb during reset
clause_matrix.acceptance: At every edge with i_reset=1, post o_scyc and o_sstb must be 0, otherwise dut_violation. Master CYC or STB high during reset is an environment violation. Reset is the only sound epoch boundary: it discards all live identities, canceled identities and hypotheses.
clause_matrix.exclusions: o_mack and o_merr after reset are not judged, because the WB slave-role reset output requirement is not explicit for the DUT. Minimum reset length is an environment property.

clause_matrix.observables: Master acceptance: i_mcyc&i_mstb&!o_mstall in pre. Slave acceptance: o_scyc&o_sstb&!i_sstall in pre.
clause_matrix.acceptance: Identity is the tuple (WE, full address, full SEL, write data on SEL-enabled lanes only). Undefined active payload is an environment violation on master inputs and a DUT violation on slave outputs.
clause_matrix.exclusions: Payload while STB is low is ignored.

clause_matrix.observables: o_saddr slice s at slave acceptance
clause_matrix.acceptance: decode(a) must equal s. An unmapped address must never be forwarded.

clause_matrix.status: inferred (an interconnect forwards only master-originated work)
clause_matrix.observables: Slave acceptance events versus the multiset of unforwarded live or canceled identities in the epoch
clause_matrix.acceptance: Every slave acceptance must consume exactly one identity-equal entry in at least one feasible hypothesis. Otherwise dut_violation. Each entry may be consumed at most once.
clause_matrix.exclusions: No claim about which of several identical entries was consumed.

clause_matrix.observables: Relative slave-acceptance order of one master's requests, both across slaves and within one slave
clause_matrix.acceptance: NOT judged. The prior P2 'oldest unforwarded head' rule is withdrawn. Response order does not imply forward order, because a DUT may buffer and reorder internally.
clause_matrix.exclusions: Global and per-master forward order. These are offered only as a characterization obligation (C3).

clause_matrix.source: README 188-196 'ACK responses won't get crossed'; WB B4 3.1.3.2 'N ACKs terminate N transactions'
clause_matrix.acceptance: Each response retires that master's oldest outstanding accepted request. Labels that depend on K6 must cite 'inferred'.
clause_matrix.exclusions: Responses while master CYC=0 are not attributable (WB B4 3.1.2).

clause_matrix.source: WB B4 obs 3.10, 3.1.3.2 'read data valid with ACK'; README
clause_matrix.status: normative for data validity; inferred for end-to-end preservation
clause_matrix.observables: i_sack/i_sdata on the slave side, matched by hypothesis to the slave-queue entry; o_mack/o_mdata on the master
clause_matrix.acceptance: A master ACK requires the retired entry to have been forwarded and slave-ACKed in the same hypothesis. For reads, o_mdata must equal the i_sdata of that slave ACK. The full 32 bits are compared for reads, because SEL does not mask read data in B4 text.
clause_matrix.exclusions: Write ACK carries no data check.

clause_matrix.source: WB B4 perm 3.20, rule 3.45; crossbar article (unmapped -> ERR); wbxbar.v header 32-39
clause_matrix.status: normative: ACK/ERR exclusivity; inferred: decode ERR and slave-ERR propagation; unknown: exact timeout/starvation conditions
clause_matrix.observables: o_merr, i_serr, decode of the entry
clause_matrix.acceptance: An ACK on an unmapped or slave-ERRed entry is a violation. An ERR on a slave-ACKed entry is a violation. An ERR on a mapped, unforwarded or un-ERRed entry is unexplained_mapped_err (unresolved, property-local).
clause_matrix.exclusions: No timeout latency. The master's reaction to ERR is not judged.

clause_matrix.source: WB B4 3.1.2/rule 3.30; crossbar article abort prose (supplementary)
clause_matrix.status: inferred: no attribution of responses across a master CYC drop; unknown: survivor set, propagation latency, residual forward order
clause_matrix.observables: i_mcyc falling with outstanding entries; later slave acceptances and responses
clause_matrix.acceptance: On a master CYC drop, unforwarded entries become canceled identities. Forwarded entries become orphan-pending. A later slave acceptance matching a canceled identity is legal-unknown: it is tagged unresolved post_abort_forward on that branch only. Responses to orphan or canceled work must never be retired into the master's new work; that is a violation in every hypothesis where it occurs. Canceled identities persist until reset.
clause_matrix.exclusions: Idle o_scyc/o_sstb and quiet slaves never discard canceled identities. There is no grace period and no delay bound.

clause_matrix.source: WB B4 3.1.3.2 ('waits' while STALL), rule 3.45, rule 3.25
clause_matrix.status: normative for the DUT acting as master to slaves
clause_matrix.observables: o_s* across a stalled cycle; o_sstb versus o_scyc; o_mack&o_merr
clause_matrix.acceptance: A violation if the DUT changes or withdraws a stalled slave request without dropping CYC, raises STB without CYC, or asserts ACK and ERR together.

clause_matrix.observables: master hold, slave in-order responses, no unsolicited response, slave cancel on CYC drop
clause_matrix.acceptance: Violations are recorded separately and yield input_or_scope_invalid. They are never reported as DUT faults.
Pending work yields pending_at_batch_end (unresolved). It is never a liveness failure.

ownership_algorithm.model: Nondeterministic reference checked as trace acceptance. State is a set H of hypotheses for the current epoch.
hypothesis_contents: per-master FIFO of entries: identity, state (new/fwd/sacked/serr/canceled/orphan), read data, uncertainty tags
per-slave FIFO of entry references, or 'orphan'
consumption status of each canceled identity

step.slave_acceptance: Branch on every eligible entry (live or canceled, any master, any position) whose identity equals the accepted request. Canceled branches get tag K9_post_abort_forward.
step.slave_response: Bind the response to the head of the slave FIFO in each hypothesis.
step.master_response: Retire the oldest entry per K6 and apply K7/K8. A hypothesis that fails a K-check is removed and the failure is recorded as a witness.

verdict_semantics.detail: Report the earliest cycle at which the last hypothesis died, with the per-branch failure witnesses. This is sound for the nondeterministic reference: no legal history explains the trace.

verdict_semantics.case: H nonempty and every surviving hypothesis depends on an unknown-status clause (a K9 tag or unexplained ERR)
H nonempty and at least one surviving hypothesis is tag-free

ownership_algorithm.owner_claims: Ownership is reported per entry as 'unique' only if all surviving hypotheses agree; otherwise it is 'indistinguishable(k candidates)'. Consistency is never presented as proof of hidden ownership.

sound_reductions.name: partitioning
sound_reductions.rule: Hypotheses factor into independent components linked only by shared identity candidates. Unrelated traffic stays in singleton components and keeps being checked.

sound_reductions.name: symmetry quotient
sound_reductions.rule: Entries with equal identity, same master, same state and no bound data are interchangeable. Store them canonically sorted, an exact quotient. Binding read data breaks the symmetry.

sound_reductions.name: component closure
sound_reductions.rule: A component closes when all its entries are retired or the epoch resets. Its tags then become final records.

ownership_algorithm.on_limit: Mark the component unresolved_on_limit with its entries and cycle. Stop judging only the clauses that depend on that component's entries: K4 for its identities, K6/K7 for masters with an entry in it. Do not prune. Continue all other components and masters. The component is released at reset, at which point checking of affected masters resumes. Never select a branch.
ownership_algorithm.resume_rule: A master's order and data checks resume after an ambiguity component closes. Distinct later work is checked even inside the same epoch.
ownership_algorithm.cumulative_records: post_abort_forward, unexplained_mapped_err and unresolved_on_limit persist across reset within the batch.

version_independent_safety.prop: Slave acceptance on s implies decode(o_saddr[s]) == s, and no slave acceptance carries an unmapped address.
version_independent_safety.evidence: unbounded prove (k-induction); bmc depth reported separately

version_independent_safety.prop: A ghost multiset over master-accepted identities in the epoch (live and canceled) must contain each slave-accepted identity, removed once. Use a symbolic-identity counter: for a free constant identity X, count(slave X) <= count(master X).
version_independent_safety.evidence: prove via induction with an auxiliary counter invariant; bmc only if induction fails, labeled bounded
version_independent_safety.cover: X forwarded twice from two masters
version_independent_safety.false_control: assert count(slave X) < count(master X) when a forward exists; it must fail

version_independent_safety.prop: Tracked symbolic transaction T: free choice of master m and a nondeterministic acceptance index. The DUT response retiring T's position equals ERR iff T is unmapped or slave-ERRed. For a read, o_mdata equals the slave data of T's forward, where the forward is identified by a ghost tag carried on the slave side through ghost FIFOs keyed by slave acceptance.
version_independent_safety.env: K11 slave in-order responses and no unsolicited responses
cover: T is a read crossing slaves with a younger forward first
version_independent_safety.false_control: mutated property expecting the younger transaction's data; it must fail with a cex

version_independent_safety.prop: A master response retiring a new-epoch entry (accepted after a CYC drop or reset) is never based on a slave response to a pre-drop or pre-reset forward. Ghost epoch bit on the slave-FIFO tags. Covers read data and write ACK in the new epoch.
version_independent_safety.env: K11 slaves cancel on CYC drop
version_independent_safety.cover: abort with orphan in flight, then new read ACK
version_independent_safety.false_control: assert no new-epoch ACK ever occurs; it must fail, showing nonvacuity

version_independent_safety.prop: After a reset edge, o_scyc and o_sstb are 0.
version_independent_safety.false_control: assert o_scyc=1 after reset; it must fail

version_independent_safety.prop: Slave-side hold under stall; never o_sstb without o_scyc; never o_mack&o_merr.
version_independent_safety.false_control: assert never stalled; it must fail

version_independent_safety.prop: Any slave acceptance after a master CYC drop either matches a ghost canceled identity (any position) or a live one.
version_independent_safety.cover: some residual forward exists, without asserting its legality
version_independent_safety.false_control: assert a residual never matches; it must fail if the cover is hit

formal_obligations.notes: Each assert gets a reachable cover; an unreached cover marks the assert vacuous and evidence-void. Environment assumptions are listed per property and are never assumed of DUT outputs. No assertion appears in assume form. BMC results state depth. Prove claims require induction success.

implementation_specific_characterization.question: Does a k exist such that no master-m-sourced forward occurs more than k cycles after a CYC drop with no new acceptance?
implementation_specific_characterization.method: cover search to find the max observed k, then attempt to prove for that k
implementation_specific_characterization.use: Only certified results may later enable discarding identities. A certificate requires a freeze and review. Never a guessed bound.

implementation_specific_characterization.question: Which buffered entries survive partial propagation?
Is per-master forward order (per slave, across slaves) preserved?
implementation_specific_characterization.use: Characterization only. Not a contract claim unless certified and separately registered.

implementation_specific_characterization.question: Does a mapped ERR without a slave ERR occur only when OPT_TIMEOUT or starvation conditions hold?
implementation_specific_characterization.use: May later reclassify unexplained_mapped_err with a certificate.

synthetic_control_assessments.name: cross_slave/early_forward_ordered_retirement
synthetic_control_assessments.assessment: M0 reads 0x05 (slave0) then 0x15 (slave1). Slave1 is forwarded first. Slave ACK data: 0x98765432 on slave1, 0x1234ABCD on slave0. Master retires 0x1234ABCD then 0x98765432, which is correct per K6/K7. The prior checker wrongly reported a routing_payload violation.
synthetic_control_assessments.label: scoped_pass
synthetic_control_assessments.basis: K5 is unknown, so forward order is not judged. K6 is inferred. The pass covers order and data only and makes no forward-order claim.

synthetic_control_assessments.name: cross_slave/wrong_retirement_data
synthetic_control_assessments.assessment: Same trace, but the first master ACK delivers 0x98765432, which is the younger request's data.
synthetic_control_assessments.label: dut_violation
synthetic_control_assessments.basis: No hypothesis survives K6+K7. The label rests on inferred K6 (README) and must be stated as such.

synthetic_control_assessments.name: ambiguity/identical_requests_later_responses
synthetic_control_assessments.assessment: Both masters read 0x05. Two forwards occur. Slave data is 0x1234ABCD then 0x98765432. M0 gets the first, m1 the second.
synthetic_control_assessments.label: scoped_pass
synthetic_control_assessments.basis: The hypothesis with forward1 owned by m1 dies because m1 would need 0x1234ABCD. One surviving hypothesis remains. Ownership is reported as 'unique by elimination under the reference', not as proof of hidden state.

synthetic_control_assessments.name: ambiguity/followed_by_distinct_work
synthetic_control_assessments.assessment: The later distinct read 0x07 returns 0x88888877, which is correct.
synthetic_control_assessments.label: scoped_pass
synthetic_control_assessments.basis: The component closed and checking resumed. The whole epoch is not disabled.

synthetic_control_assessments.name: ambiguity/later_data_corruption
synthetic_control_assessments.assessment: The later read delivers 0x88888876 while the slave returned 0x88888877.
synthetic_control_assessments.label: dut_violation
synthetic_control_assessments.basis: The singleton component fails in all hypotheses.

synthetic_control_assessments.name: ambiguity/later_unaccepted_address
synthetic_control_assessments.assessment: The 0x07 request is forwarded as 0x0C. 0x0C routes legally to slave0, but no live or canceled identity matches it.
synthetic_control_assessments.label: dut_violation
synthetic_control_assessments.basis: K4 fails in all hypotheses. The later ACK is irrelevant to the label.

synthetic_control_assessments.name: ambiguity/inherently_indistinguishable
synthetic_control_assessments.assessment: Both slave ACKs carry 0x1234ABCD, so both hypotheses survive.
synthetic_control_assessments.label: scoped_pass
synthetic_control_assessments.basis: Observable clauses hold under every feasible history. Ownership is reported as indistinguishable(2). No hidden-owner claim is made. The label is not 'unresolved', because no unknown clause is relied on.

synthetic_control_assessments.name: prior selftests retained
tests: enabled-byte corrupt and double consumption -> violation
synthetic_control_assessments.assessment: All labels remain justified under the new model. abort_none_forwarded_pass stays scoped_pass: unforwarded canceled identities are legal and are not pending obligations. Note that this does not certify empty buffers.

synthetic_control_assessments.name: prior inferred rule withdrawn
synthetic_control_assessments.assessment: P2's 'oldest unforwarded head' was the wrongly inferred expectation. It caused cross-slave early forwarding to be labeled a violation and is removed.

synthetic_control_assessments.name: new controls to add
controls: Same-master identical reads to the same slave with distinct data, retired in correct order: pass.
The same with swapped data: violation.
ERR during ambiguity: m1 gets ERR while the slave ACKed both. Hypotheses die, so violation.
ERR after ambiguity on distinct mapped work with no slave ERR: unresolved, local.
Partial cancel: abort with one forwarded and one unforwarded entry; the orphan's ACK must not retire new-epoch work. Violation if it does, pass otherwise.
New-epoch read and write after abort and after reset: each checked.
Residual forward after abort that matches a canceled identity, interleaved with live identical work from the other master: unresolved only if every surviving hypothesis uses the canceled branch.
Hypothesis-limit control with a lowered test constant: unresolved_on_limit is local, and an unrelated master is still checked.
Write identical except on masked lanes: treated as equal identity.

implementation_plan: 1. Implement the checker v2 contract (K1-K12) and the hypothesis engine with partitioning, symmetry quotient, declared limits and per-clause verdicts. Keep verdict precedence env > violation > unresolved > pass, reported per clause and in aggregate.
2. Have an independent author write the controls from the clause matrix, not from checker code. This covers all controls above plus the retained prior ones.
3. Fresh code review against this matrix, including mutation checks. Each K-check is disabled in turn and must be caught by at least one control.

4. Write the formal harness: ghost FIFOs, symbolic tracked transaction, covers and false controls. Record the bmc/prove distinction. Characterization C1-C4 goes in a separate report, and any contract change requires a certificate and re-review.
5. Freeze the checker, controls and harness hashes, then perform immutable saved-action replay before live B/C.
6. Live B/C uses the original driver, budgets and traffic. No error suppression, forced reset, unique tags or one-outstanding restriction without a separately registered scope.
unresolved: Forward order (K5), the cancellation survivor set and latency (K9), and timeout/starvation eligibility (K8) are unknowable from public sources.
Hidden ownership of identical requests with identical responses is inherently indistinguishable.
Response order (K6) is inferred from README prose, not WB-normative.
No sound cancellation boundary other than reset exists without a certified C1. Canceled identities therefore persist, and residual forwards matching them stay unresolved.
DUT post-reset o_mack/o_merr and the eventual withdrawal of slave CYC after an abort remain unchecked.
Any pass is scoped to the checked clauses, the feasible-history semantics and the declared limits.
proposed_design.ready_for_implementation: true for checker v2, controls and formal harness implementation; false for live B/C until steps 2-5 are completed

cross_slave/early_forward_ordered_retire.proposed: must not report violation solely for cross-slave forwarding order; architect decides supported scoped pass vs unresolved

cross_slave/wrong_retirement_data.proposed: detect wrong returned data/order; distinct data makes the fault externally observable

ambiguity/identical_requests_later_respo.proposed: keep feasible ownership candidates; explicitly distinguish observable trace consistency from hidden-owner proof

ambiguity/followed_by_distinct_work.proposed: do not disable checking of independent subsequent work for the whole reset epoch

ambiguity/later_data_corruption.proposed: detect uniquely observable new read-data corruption despite previous ambiguity

ambiguity/later_unaccepted_address.proposed: detect a forward with no valid live or canceled identity; previous ambiguity cannot hide it

ambiguity/inherently_indistinguishable.proposed: do not claim actual ownership uniquely established; identical observations cannot supply absent transaction tags

additional_existing_synthetic_case.name: multi_abort/live_aborted_same_identity
additional_existing_synthetic_case.note: Independent synthetic control, not a DUT or LLM trace; no verdict supplied.

integration_questions.question: The proposal calls a trace consistent when at least one surviving history is tag-free, even if other viable histories use unknown cancellation. Define separate observable trace-membership, universal checked-property, and hidden-ownership claims. Can this ever promote an unresolved obligation to a stronger pass? Include the old-live identical-identity case and persist uncertainty without guessing an owner.

Equal identity, same master/state and unbound data do not by themselves demonstrate a symmetry when FIFO positions differ (e.g. A,B,A). Require a bisimulation or canonical renaming preserving all master/slave order edges, references, multiplicity and future data bindings; do not sort away temporal order.

Shared payload identity is not the only dependency. Master retirement FIFO, slave response FIFO and epoch/cancellation state also couple distinct identities. Define a sound dependency closure and prove local checking/resource-limit fallback does not miss a reachable dependency.

F3/F4 attach ghost tags to a slave acceptance although physical Wishbone carries no transaction ID. Define how tags are assigned independently, how that assignment is validated, and whether nondeterministic choices are universally or existentially quantified. Do not use an assumed correct mapping to prove correct mapping.

C1 with no new acceptance may bound only the quiet interval. It cannot automatically erase identities before future restart, nor does empty output imply empty buffers. Require a restart-safe noninterference claim before releasing old work. Address repeated aborts and avoid one-bit epoch aliasing.

F3 ERR iff unmapped or slave-ERRed appears stronger than K8, which keeps timeout/starvation unexplained errors unknown. Make guards/unknown cases consistent. Also specify widths/overflow invariants for cumulative symbolic counters; an unbounded proof cannot quietly rely on the finite pilot horizon.

K5 withdraws both across-slave and within-slave forward order. Assess old same-slave reordered-write controls separately: public ordering/side-effect assumptions must be explicit. Identify changes before any experimental replay; do not force legacy labels or quietly weaken required data/response guarantees.

isolation: No DUT RTL or actual pin traces, version-specific proof results, prior B/C metrics, coverage groups, witness targeting or experimental model prompts.
